note: Sector definitions for the chart generator (S3.1, D-104; lanes and crossings since H.6, D-193 to D-199). A sector is a band of space crossed from an origin port on the left to a delivery port on the right, in columns. `nodes` is the range of points on the chart, `columns` the range of columns they sit in (origin and delivery are columns of their own). `kinds` weights what each point in between is; `minimum` makes sure each kind turns up at least that often. `hazards` are the names a hazard point is given. `designations` are the letter codes on Margo's company chart. `fuel` is the start and the tank; a lane costs 1 fuel, 2 for a long one. `hours` is how long a lane is: `base`, plus `column` for each column it crosses, plus `climb` times how far it climbs up or down the chart (0 to 1), rounded, from `min` to `max`, then times its risk's `length`. `slack` is the spare time on the deadline, a share of the cheapest way across in hours (the deadline is that way's hours times one and the slack). `union` is how deep the band of Outer Stations Union space is, top or bottom of the chart (a share of its height). `risks` are what a lane can hold, in order: the first whose `where` fits a lane is its risk (`touches` a kind of point; `beacon` a lane to the old company beacon, set on one open-space point; `union` both ends in Union space; `default` anything left). A risk's `contacts` is the chance an hour that a ship turns up on the scope while we cross it, `aboard` the chance an hour that something happens aboard (a situation from the events that fit the point the lane runs to, on top of that point's own dice; H.8), `encounters` the weights of which one (content/encounters/), `strikes` an hourly chance of being hit by `weapon` (a pilot at the helm sees most of it coming), `length` what it does to the lane's hours. `pursuit` is the chance a run's contract is followed, which encounter follows, how many hours `lead` it gives us before it can turn up, and `rate`, the chance an hour after that that it finds us; driven off by the gun it gives up, any other way it picks the trail up again after its lead. `events` is the chance that passing each kind of point for the first time brings a transit event, somewhere along the lane that runs to it (S3.3; H.7 makes these situations aboard).

risks.name: Patrol lane
risks.label: Patrol
risks.text: Receivers' cutters work this line out of the checkpoint. They stop what they find and go through the hold.

risks.name: Dead station
risks.label: Wreck
risks.text: Something died out here and is still being picked over. Whoever is picking does not want company.

risks.name: Hazard
risks.label: Hazard
risks.text: Bad space. Things in it hit the hull, and the helm has to see them coming. Few ships come this way.

risks.name: Company beacon
risks.label: Beacon
risks.text: An old company beacon still calls the line. It is the quickest way through, and everyone listening knows a ship is on it.

risks.name: Union space
risks.label: Union
risks.text: The Outer Stations Union holds this side of the Reach. Its bulwarks charge for the lanes and its drones count who uses them.

risks.name: Open lane
risks.label: Open
risks.text: Nothing on the chart. That is not the same as nothing out there.
